inspect-grounding.title: Inspect the grounding
inspect-grounding.prompt: Mark each item safe or a hazard.

config.scene: A station on the third floor of a house.

items.label: Every chassis is wired to one single-point ground.
items.why: One reference point keeps everything at the same potential.

items.label: Each radio has its own separate ground rod, not bonded to the others.
items.why: Unbonded rods can sit at different voltages in a lightning strike. Bond them together.

items.label: A 20 A fuse replaces the 10 A one the manual specifies.
items.why: In a fault it won't blow in time. Damage or fire can follow.

items.label: The ground rod is copper-clad steel.
items.why: The best choice: strong and conductive.

items.label: The line cord's green wire goes to the chassis.
items.why: If a fault touches the chassis, the current goes to ground.

items.label: Filter capacitors are discharged with a screwdriver.
items.why: Use an insulated shorting stick with an inline resistor.

items.label: A 10 m wire down to the ground rod is the station's only RF ground.
items.why: On HF it can have high impedance: you can get RF burns from the equipment.
